stories.title: Migrate messaging-limits tier model to 100K flat cap (Q2 2026)
stories.description: Meta is removing the 2K and 10K daily messaging limit tiers in Q2 2026; any verified business immediately receives 100K/day. The existing messaging-limits.ts still models tiers '250', '2000', '10000', '100000'. The admin tier selector and in-app messaging-limit display must be updated to reflect the new flat-cap model and remove obsolete lower tiers.
acceptanceCriteria: TIER_LIMITS constant in messaging-limits.ts removes '250' and '2000' tiers
PUT /analytics/messaging-limits/tier returns 400 if tier '250' or '2000' is supplied
Admin UI tier dropdown shows only '10000', '100000', and 'unlimited' as selectable options
Existing rows in app_settings table with value '250' or '2000' are auto-migrated to '10000' on startup
Vitest unit test asserts 200 response for valid tiers and 400 for removed tiers
technicalNotes: Source: Meta developer docs — https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/upcoming-messaging-limits-changes/
Migration must be backward-compatible; if DB row is missing, default to '100000' not '250'
Admin notification should be sent once when auto-migration executes

stories.title: WhatsApp portfolio pacing monitor: detect and alert when batch delivery is paused
stories.description: Meta's portfolio pacing silently pauses bulk template sends mid-campaign when quality signals (blocks, complaints) are negative. There is currently no mechanism in Rainbow AI to detect that a scheduled send was paused or that quality feedback triggered a hold, meaning operators discover delivery failures only after the fact.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /analytics/messaging-limits returns a pacingPaused: boolean field derived from Meta Graph API quality signals
When pacingPaused is true, admin dashboard displays a visible warning banner
Admin notification is sent within 5 minutes of a pacing pause being detected
Alert body includes the affected template name and percentage of batch not yet delivered
Vitest test mocks the Meta quality signal endpoint and asserts the correct pacingPaused state is surfaced
technicalNotes: Poll Meta's WABA health/quality endpoint: GET /{phone-number-id}/quality_rating
Store last known pacing state in app_settings to avoid repeated notifications
Reference: https://www.fyno.io/blog/how-does-whatsapp-template-pacing-work-a-detailed-guide-cm2tykayw00d7wixo00hhiuxk
dependencies: Migrate messaging-limits tier model to 100K flat cap (Q2 2026)

stories.title: WABA webhook subscription health check on server startup
stories.description: Meta's developer experience change in late 2025 means the WABA-to-App webhook subscription can fail silently: the webhook URL is verified but the app never actually receives events. Rainbow AI has no startup check that confirms the WABA subscription is active, so a silently broken subscription could cause all inbound WhatsApp messages to go missing without any alert.
acceptanceCriteria: On server startup, a check calls GET /{waba-id}/subscribed_apps and confirms the app is subscribed
If the subscription is missing, the check automatically resubscribes via POST /{waba-id}/subscribed_apps
Admin notification is sent if auto-resubscription fails
Health endpoint GET /health returns webhookSubscribed: true|false
The check is skipped gracefully when WABA credentials are absent (e.g., development environment)
Vitest test mocks the Meta Graph API and asserts resubscription is attempted when subscription is absent
technicalNotes: Use the existing Meta Graph API token stored in env vars
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices
Subscription check should run once on startup and then every 6 hours via setInterval

stories.title: Persist raw webhook payloads to durable storage before processing
stories.description: Best practice for WhatsApp Cloud API webhook reliability requires logging every raw payload to durable storage before any processing so that lost or failed events can be replayed. Currently, Rainbow AI processes messages directly in-memory after BullMQ dequeues them; if processing fails mid-flight and the DLQ entry lacks the original raw payload, the message is unrecoverable.
acceptanceCriteria: Every inbound webhook payload is written to a webhook_raw_events table (or S3 object) before the BullMQ job is enqueued
Each raw event row includes: event_id UUID, received_at timestamp, profile, payload JSONB, processed BOOLEAN
The DLQ entry references the raw event ID so operators can replay the original payload
GET /admin/dlq/:jobId returns the associated raw event payload
Vitest test asserts raw event is persisted even when downstream processing throws
technicalNotes: Insert should be a fire-and-forget with its own try/catch to avoid blocking the webhook 200 response
Retention policy: raw events should be pruned by the existing data-retention scheduler after 30 days
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: WhatsApp media auto-download: save incoming images/documents before URL expiry
stories.description: WhatsApp temporary media URLs provided via webhooks expire after 24-48 hours. Currently, Rainbow AI receives image and document messages but does not eagerly download and persist the binary content. If a guest sends a photo of their ID or a booking confirmation document and the URL expires before a staff member views it, the media is permanently lost.
acceptanceCriteria: When a Baileys message event contains imageMessage, documentMessage, or videoMessage, the binary is downloaded immediately
Downloaded file is stored on disk (or S3) under a path keyed by message ID
The conversation message record in rainbow_messages is updated with a localMediaUrl field
If the download fails, a retry is attempted up to 3 times with exponential backoff before logging to DLQ
Admin conversation view renders the locally-stored URL, not the ephemeral WhatsApp URL
Vitest test mocks the download call and asserts the localMediaUrl field is populated
technicalNotes: Use Baileys downloadMediaMessage() helper: it handles decryption automatically
Store under ./media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<messageId>.<ext> and serve via a static Express route
Reference: https://wasenderapi.com/blog/how-to-receive-whatsapp-messages-via-webhook-the-ultimate-2025-guide

stories.title: Webchat widget dark mode support via CSS prefers-color-scheme
stories.description: The webchat widget currently has a single light-mode color scheme. Cafe customers ordering on mobile at night experience harsh white backgrounds; dark mode via prefers-color-scheme media queries would improve comfort and match system preferences, consistent with 2025 chat UI standards.
acceptanceCriteria: Widget CSS includes a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block that inverts the background/text palette
Dark mode applies to the chat bubble, header bar, message list, and input field
Widget embed script accepts an optional theme: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto' config parameter
When theme is 'auto', the widget follows the OS preference dynamically
No flash of unstyled content (FOUC) on load — theme class is applied before first paint
Playwright visual test captures dark-mode screenshot on a simulated dark-mode browser
technicalNotes: Add CSS custom properties (variables) for all palette tokens to minimize duplication
Existing rainbow-theme.css already has a dark-mode section for the admin panel — widget CSS should follow the same token naming
Reference: https://lollypop.design/blog/2025/january/chatbot-ui-ux-design-best-practices-examples/

stories.title: AI waiter returning-customer order history: suggest last order on session start
stories.description: Restaurant chatbot best practice for 2025 is to recognize returning customers and proactively suggest their previous order, increasing conversion and average ticket size. Currently, the Makan Moments AI waiter has no mechanism to look up past orders for a webchat session.
acceptanceCriteria: On webchat session start, if the session identifier matches a prior order in the database, a 'Welcome back! Order your usual again?' quick-reply button appears
Clicking the quick-reply populates the cart with the most recent completed order for that session/customer
If the prior order contains out-of-stock items, those are omitted and the customer is notified
The feature is opt-in per profile and can be disabled via admin settings toggle
Vitest test confirms the last-order lookup returns empty for first-time sessions and the correct prior cart for returning sessions
technicalNotes: Customer identity: use the webchat session ID or a local-storage UUID — no account registration required
Query: SELECT items FROM fnb_orders WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
Reference: https://botpress.com/blog/chatbot-for-restaurants (returning customer personalization section)

stories.title: Admin dashboard multi-user RBAC: viewer vs operator vs super-admin roles
stories.description: The current admin system has a single flat admin user model. As the business scales with multiple staff managing different properties, a role-based access control layer is needed so that cafe staff (viewer) cannot modify hostel system prompts, and operators cannot delete system-wide configs only super-admins should touch.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin users table gains a role column with enum: 'viewer' | 'operator' | 'super-admin'
Viewer role: read-only access to analytics and conversations; cannot POST/PUT/DELETE
Operator role: all viewer permissions plus ability to manage conversations, send messages, and update knowledge base
Super-admin role: all operator permissions plus user management, profile configuration, and data deletion
Role is enforced server-side via Express middleware; missing role returns 403
POST /auth/register accepts a role field; defaults to 'viewer' if omitted
Vitest test asserts 403 when a viewer token attempts a PUT on config
technicalNotes: Add role to adminUsers Drizzle schema; run db:push migration
Middleware: checkRole(['operator', 'super-admin']) applied to mutating routes
Reference: https://www.techprescient.com/blogs/role-based-access-control-best-practices/
Principle of least privilege: default all existing users to 'operator' during migration to avoid lockout

stories.title: LLM response faithfulness check: flag answers that contradict the knowledge base
stories.description: Rainbow AI performs Zod schema validation and structured retries on LLM responses but has no semantic check that the answer is grounded in KB content. In production, LLMs can generate plausible-sounding but factually wrong hostel policies. A post-generation faithfulness check would catch hallucinations before the response is sent.
acceptanceCriteria: After generating a KB-backed answer, a secondary check verifies key facts in the answer appear in the retrieved KB chunks
If faithfulness score < 0.7 and a KB chunk exists, the answer is replaced with a conservative 'please check with our team' fallback
faithfulness_score is logged in intent_analytics for monitoring
Admin analytics dashboard shows a 'Low faithfulness rate' KPI (% of answers flagged) for the past 7 days
The check adds no more than 500ms to response time
Vitest test: inject a KB chunk with 'check-in: 2pm' and assert a response containing 'check-in: 3pm' is flagged
technicalNotes: Lightweight approach: extract key noun phrases from response, confirm each appears verbatim or semantically in the top-k retrieved chunks
Expensive approach: second LLM call with 'Does the answer contradict the context? YES/NO'
Reference: https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/llm-hallucination-detection-and-mitigation-best-techniques/
Start with lightweight approach; gate the expensive approach behind a feature flag

stories.title: WhatsApp template rejection monitoring: detect and alert on REJECTED or PAUSED status
stories.description: The existing template-quality.ts route tracks phone quality ratings, but there is no automated check that polls template status from Meta and alerts when a previously approved template is REJECTED or PAUSED. Operators could be silently sending a paused template with no delivery and no notification.
acceptanceCriteria: A scheduled job (every 4 hours) polls GET /{waba-id}/message_templates for each profile and records status in a whatsapp_templates table
When a template transitions from APPROVED to REJECTED or PAUSED, an admin notification is sent including the template name and rejection reason code
GET /admin/templates returns the list with current status, last checked timestamp, and rejection code if applicable
Admin UI shows a red badge on the Templates tab when any template is in REJECTED or PAUSED state
Vitest test mocks the Meta template list endpoint and asserts notification fires on REJECTED status
technicalNotes: Meta Graph API: GET /{whatsapp-business-account-id}/message_templates?fields=name,status,rejected_reason
Common rejection codes: PROMOTIONAL_CONTENT, VARIABLE_PARAMETERS, DUPLICATE_MESSAGE
Reference: https://www.infobip.com/docs/whatsapp/compliance/template-compliance
Store template statuses in Postgres; alert only on status transitions (not every poll)

stories.title: PDPA 2024 Phase 3: machine-readable data portability export with CSV and self-service OTP
stories.description: Malaysia's PDPA Amendment Act 2024 Phase 3 (June 2025) introduced the right to data portability requiring structured, machine-readable formats on request. The existing data export returns JSON but lacks CSV format and a self-service customer-facing route with OTP verification as required for compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/rainbow/guests/:jid/data-export?format=json returns existing JSON (no change)
GET /api/rainbow/guests/:jid/data-export?format=csv returns all message data as RFC 4180-compliant CSV with BOM for Excel compatibility
Both formats include: timestamp, direction (inbound/outbound), message content, intent, sentiment
A publicly documented endpoint (not behind admin auth) allows guests to request their own data using their phone number + a one-time verification code sent via WhatsApp
The export request is logged to gdpr_audit_log with action='portability'
Vitest test asserts CSV output parses correctly with 100% field coverage and no formula-injection characters
technicalNotes: CSV must not contain formula-injection characters (=, +, -, @) at the start of fields
OTP verification for self-service: send a WhatsApp message with a 6-digit code, valid 10 minutes
Reference: https://hhq.com.my/posts/full-implementation-of-the-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-final-roundup/
Phase 3 effective June 1, 2025 — this is already overdue

stories.title: Chatbot conversation containment rate KPI on admin analytics dashboard
stories.description: The admin analytics panel tracks CSAT and resolution rates but is missing the deflection/containment rate — the percentage of conversations fully resolved by the bot without human escalation. This is the single most-cited chatbot ROI metric in 2025 analytics best practices.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /analytics/kpis returns a containmentRate field: (conversations without escalation) / (total conversations) x 100
Containment rate is shown as a percentage card on the admin dashboard with 24h, 7d, and 30d views
A trend sparkline shows daily containment rate over the past 30 days
Drill-down: clicking the metric lists conversation IDs where the bot failed to contain (i.e., escalated)
An alert threshold in admin settings triggers a notification when containment rate drops below a configurable % (default 70%)
Vitest test seeds 10 conversations (7 contained, 3 escalated) and asserts containmentRate = 70
technicalNotes: Contained = no escalation_events row for that conversation_id within the session
Join rainbow_conversations with escalation_events to compute metric
Reference: https://quickchat.ai/post/chatbot-analytics

stories.title: AI waiter order accuracy rate KPI: track and display correct vs corrected orders
stories.description: Best-in-class restaurant chatbots target 95%+ order accuracy. Rainbow AI currently has no metric tracking how often a customer corrects an order after the AI waiter confirms it. Tracking post-confirmation corrections would reveal whether the order-taking flow is producing errors.
acceptanceCriteria: An order_correction event is recorded whenever a customer modifies the cart after receiving an AI order confirmation message
GET /analytics/kpis returns orderAccuracyRate: (orders with no post-confirm correction) / (total confirmed orders) x 100
Admin dashboard shows order accuracy rate as a KPI card alongside CSAT
If accuracy rate drops below 90%, an admin alert is triggered
Vitest test: simulate 10 orders with 2 post-confirm corrections and assert rate = 80%
technicalNotes: Order confirmation event already fires on cart confirmation intent; add a correction_event that triggers on any cart-modify intent AFTER an order_confirmed event in the same session
Reference: https://hostie.ai/resources/best-ai-chatbots-restaurant-websites-takeout-orders-2025
Store events in intent_analytics table with event_type: 'order_confirmed' | 'order_corrected'

stories.title: LLM provider cost budget alert: notify when daily spend exceeds configurable threshold
stories.description: The existing llm-cost-budget.ts tracks LLM token costs, but there is no proactive admin alert when daily spend approaches or exceeds a configured budget limit. Without alerts, runaway usage (e.g., a looping tool call or traffic spike) could accumulate large LLM costs before anyone notices.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin settings accepts a llmDailyBudgetUsd value (default: $10.00)
A check runs every 30 minutes; when cumulative daily cost reaches 80% of budget, an admin warning notification is sent
When cumulative daily cost reaches 100% of budget, an admin critical alert is sent and new LLM calls are rate-limited to 1 per 30 seconds per JID
Budget resets at UTC midnight
GET /analytics/llm-cost returns currentDayUsd, budgetUsd, and budgetPctUsed
Vitest test mocks daily spend at 81% and asserts warning notification fires exactly once
technicalNotes: Build on existing llm-cost-budget.ts — add threshold comparison logic and notification call
Use admin-notifier.ts sendAlert() for the notification
Rate-limit fallback should use a simple in-memory token bucket, not a hard block (to avoid breaking emergency messages)

stories.title: Webchat widget progressive disclosure onboarding for first-time visitors
stories.description: UX research for 2025 shows users decide within 5 seconds whether to engage with a chatbot, and progressive disclosure of functionality significantly improves engagement. The Makan Moments webchat widget currently opens to an empty chat; adding a structured first-message with quick-reply buttons for first-time visitors would increase session engagement rates.
acceptanceCriteria: On first open (no prior session history), the widget auto-displays a greeting message with 3 quick-reply buttons
Button options are configurable per profile via admin settings (label + intent payload)
The greeting message respects the profile's configured bot name and persona
Subsequent opens (returning session) skip the onboarding greeting and restore conversation history
The feature can be toggled off per profile via an admin settings boolean
Playwright test verifies onboarding buttons appear on first load and are absent on second load
technicalNotes: Detect first visit via localStorage key 'rainbow_session_started'
Quick-reply buttons post a predefined intent payload to the webchat-api — same mechanism as existing quick replies
Reference: https://www.netguru.com/blog/chatbot-ux-tips (progressive disclosure section)

stories.title: Admin API endpoint-specific rate limiting: stricter limits on auth routes vs read routes
stories.description: Express security best practices for 2025 require endpoint-specific rate limits: authentication endpoints must have far stricter limits than read-only analytics endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks. The current rate-limit-settings.ts appears to apply a global rate limit with no differentiation between /auth/login and /analytics/*.
acceptanceCriteria: A strict rate limiter (5 requests per minute per IP) is applied to all /auth/* routes
A standard rate limiter (60 requests per minute per IP) is applied to all /analytics/* and read-only GET routes
429 responses from the auth limiter include a Retry-After header
Rate limit metadata (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) is returned on all rate-limited routes
Vitest test: fire 6 rapid requests to /auth/login from the same IP and assert the 6th returns 429
technicalNotes: Use express-rate-limit with differentiated windowMs and max per route group
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/blog/securing-apis-express-rate-limit-and-slow-down/
The existing rate-limit-settings.ts admin UI can expose the per-route limit values for operator adjustment

stories.title: WhatsApp template category auto-validator: warn on rejection risk before submission
stories.description: Since July 2025, Meta auto-reclassifies utility templates containing promotional intent as marketing templates, changing cost and delivery characteristics. Rainbow AI allows admins to create and submit templates via the admin UI but has no pre-submission validator that checks for common rejection triggers.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin template editor shows inline warnings when the template body contains promotional keywords (e.g., 'discount', 'offer', 'buy now', 'click here')
A warning fires if the template body starts or ends with a {{variable}} placeholder
A warning fires if two templates with identical body text exist in the same profile
Warnings are non-blocking (admin can still submit) but prominently displayed
The validator runs client-side in real time as the admin types
Vitest test: assert warning count for a known-bad template (starts with variable + promotional keyword)
technicalNotes: Validator is a pure function: validateTemplate(body: string, existingTemplates: string[]) => Warning[]
Promotional keyword list should be configurable via admin settings
Reference: https://support.wati.io/en/articles/11463457-best-practices-to-avoid-template-message-rejection
Run the same function server-side on PUT /admin/templates to log a validation_warnings field to the DB

stories.title: PDPA 2024 Phase 3: mandatory DPO contact details in first-interaction data notice
stories.description: Phase 3 of Malaysia's PDPA Amendment Act (June 2025) requires organisations to appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) and make their contact details accessible to data subjects. Rainbow AI's first-interaction data notice must be updated to include a named DPO contact or privacy enquiry email.
acceptanceCriteria: The first-interaction WhatsApp notice message includes a sentence: 'For data enquiries, contact our DPO at [dpo_email from settings]'
Admin settings accepts dpoName and dpoEmail fields per profile
If dpoEmail is not configured, a validation warning is shown in the admin settings UI and a startup log warning is emitted
The webchat consent banner also includes the DPO contact link
Vitest test asserts the notice message text includes the dpoEmail value from settings
technicalNotes: DPO requirement effective June 1, 2025 per PDPA Amendment Act 2024 Phase 3
Reference: https://rajadarrylloh.com/the-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-and-guidelines-on-the-appointment-of-data-protection-officer-and-data-breach-notification/
Add dpoName and dpoEmail to the profile config schema and settings.json defaults
Per-profile DPO allows different contacts for Pelangi Capsule and Makan Moments

stories.title: WhatsApp per-message pricing: update cost model with free utility window logic
stories.description: Meta switched from Conversation-Based Pricing to Per-Message Pricing (PMP) effective July 2025 with a second update January 1, 2026. The pricing table and free-window logic must be updated: utility messages sent inside an open 24-hour service window are now free, and January 2026 added new country rate tiers for MY, SG, and US markets.
acceptanceCriteria: Cost calculator correctly returns $0.00 for utility messages sent within an active 24-hour service session
Rate table includes January 2026 revised rates for MY, SG, and US markets
GET /analytics/whatsapp-cost returns a breakdown showing messagingModel: 'per-message' (not 'per-conversation')
Admin cost dashboard labels reflect 'PMP' and links to Meta pricing docs
Vitest test covers free utility window scenario and returns cost = 0
technicalNotes: Reference: https://m.aisensy.com/blog/whatsapp-per-message-pricing-update-effective-january-1-2026/
Free service window: utility templates sent when session window is open incur $0
Store last pricing-table update date in app_settings; alert admin if table is > 90 days stale
